reasons.A: Period diction, semicolons and double dashes fit, and short declaratives mix with long ones, but the aphorisms and ornamental closing simile are more lyrical and polished than the passage's plain, emphatic manner.
reasons.B: It is closest in movement, with one long unbroken paragraph of semicolon-chained, cumulative sentences, confident superlatives, double dashes and Victorian register, though the closing questions and exclamation go slightly beyond the passage.
reasons.C: Modern, even and plain, with short, evenly weighted sentences, almost no semicolons or dashes, a neutral explanatory stance and tidy paragraphs; the passage's period rhythm and emphatic assertion are missing.
